title: Portulan Workspace Definition v2.4
description: The manifest at the root of a workspace. It is an index, not a container: it names the slots the engine resolves against and points at the Markdown that holds each slot's content and rationale. Written in a deliberately small subset of JSON Schema 2020-12 — see spec/README.md for the subset and for what validates it.

portulan.description: Version block. `spec` is the Workspace Definition version this manifest is written against; the engine uses it to decide whether a migration is needed.

spec.description: Workspace Definition version, MAJOR.MINOR. A MAJOR bump means a migration exists.

workspace.description: Optional version of this workspace's own content, SemVer. Lets a workspace shipped as a plugin be pinned by consumers.

name.description: Stable identifier for this workspace — used as a plugin name when the workspace ships through a feed.

summary.description: One line an agent can read before loading anything else.

kind.description: Which of the three workspace kinds this is. The distinction is load-bearing: a demo workspace is written to be read by strangers and must carry no real internal policy, while a repository or portfolio workspace carries exactly that.

slots.description: Path slots. Every value resolves to a file or a directory relative to the workspace root. Fragments are not permitted: a slot addressed by `#anchor` cannot be checked, so a slot's content must be a whole file. The pattern alone cannot say WHICH slot may leave the workspace directory — of the slots here only `constitution` is expected to (the sibling `tree` is the other, outside this object) — and spec/slots.md has `doctor` report (never fail) any other slot that does.

identity.description: Who this team is, the stack, and the glossary. The first thing an agent reads after the kernel.

principles.description: The team's own binding principles — the constitution slot. What makes an agent work THIS team's way rather than generically.

constitution.description: Optional. A separate document this team's work is graded against, when one exists apart from `principles`. This is the slot permitted to point outside the workspace directory, because a product's constitution usually lives with the product rather than with the workspace.

gates.description: The gate map: this team's concrete actions bound to the engine's Auto / Propose / Gated tiers, plus the triage threshold.

dod.description: Optional. The workspace's extension of core's definition-of-done floor. Absent means core's floor stands alone, which is valid.

memory.description: Optional. Directory of durable facts, one per file, each carrying provenance.

repos.description: Optional. Directory of repo cards, one per repository this workspace covers.

handoffs.description: Optional. Directory of dated handoffs, filenames leading with an ISO date.

proposals.description: Optional. Directory of agent-drafted rule changes awaiting the human gate.

verify.description: The executable half of done. A workspace declares its recipes and names the default; a repo card may override it and a task may specialize it.

default.description: The `id` of the recipe the Stop-gate runs when nothing more specific applies. Constrained to the same shape as an id, so a value no recipe could ever carry is rejected by the schema rather than only by `doctor`.

products.description: Optional. The product layer, repeated: a workspace may cover many products — a portfolio workspace covers all of a studio's — so mission/what/why and agent affordances belong to a product, not to the workspace. A workspace need not declare products at all; one that does gives an entry per product, including when there is only one.

affordances.description: Optional workspace-level default for agent affordances, inherited by any product that does not declare its own. The same more-specific-wins rule as the resolution cascade, applied inside the workspace.

tree.description: Optional. Where the repository tree this workspace makes claims ABOUT begins, relative to the workspace root — for a workspace that is the policy layer of the repository containing it, `../`. Present means `doctor` lints repo-card build/test/run and layout claims, and the gate map's required-check claim, against that tree. Absent means the workspace describes repositories not present beside it — a demo, or a portfolio spanning many — and those claims are REPORTED unverifiable rather than checked. Declared rather than inferred from `kind`: `kind` is self-declared, and a whole check class silently disabled by a self-declared field is a fail-open with a doorbell; and a portfolio workspace is not a demo yet has no single tree either, so kind-dispatch would break on its second case.

gates.description: Optional, added in 2.1. The gate POLICY — a path to a JSON file the enforcement compiler reads, distinct from `slots.gates`, which is the Markdown that argues it. Two keys rather than one because they answer different questions and only one of them compiles: `slots.gates` is prose a human reads and no tool can dispatch on, while this file binds action patterns to tiers in a host-neutral vocabulary. A workspace may declare either, both, or neither — but a workspace with prose and no policy has a gate map nothing enforces, which is the state this repository was in for three milestones and named honestly while it lasted.

packs.description: Optional. The packs this workspace composes, in cascade order — core < pack < workspace. Named here so a workspace can state which stack, tool, and ritual layers it depends on rather than leaving it to be inferred.

memory.description: Optional, added in 2.3. What the memory store's generated index is called and what memory may cost — distinct from `slots.memory`, which is the store itself, for the same reason `gates` is distinct from `slots.gates`: one is content, this is machine configuration. A workspace may declare a store and no budget, which is every workspace that existed before 2.3 and is a legitimate shape; what it may not do is declare this object without a store, since there would be nothing to index. That conditional requirement is `doctor`'s, not the schema's — the declared subset has no `dependentRequired`, exactly as with `tree` when `kind` is `repository`.

index.description: The generated index: the layer loaded to decide what else to load. It is built by `cli/index.mjs` and byte-compared by a verify recipe, so nothing in it is hand-maintained. Its path must resolve OUTSIDE `slots.memory` — an index living in the store is counted as a record by `doctor`'s store report, and `index` refuses that siting rather than teaching one filename to hide from a walk.

path.description: Where the generated index is written, relative to the workspace root.

budget.description: Optional. A rail, not an aim: on breach the remedy is consolidation — merge, compress, retire — and never a raise in the same change (core/operating/memory.md). Nothing here is defaulted; an undeclared number is not checked, because a default would be this specification setting a policy for every workspace that adopts it, in a key nobody typed.

lines.description: The most lines the generated index may hold. With one line per record this is a rail on record COUNT, which is the cost memory imposes on every recall. Must be a POSITIVE INTEGER: the subset has no `minimum`, so `type: number` is the strongest constraint expressible here and `cli/index.mjs` refuses zero, negative and non-integer values with exit 2 rather than reading them as undeclared — a budget of `0` is falsy, and would otherwise switch the rail off in the key that exists to switch it on.

columns.description: The most columns any one index line may hold. Closes the hole a line budget has — one enormous line absorbing what the budget counts — and is refused rather than truncated, since a silently shortened title is a generated file disagreeing with its source. A positive integer, on the same terms as `lines`.

store.description: Optional. Budgets on the store itself rather than on its index. The axis an index cannot see: record count can hold still while the records grow.

budget.description: Optional, and not defaulted, on the same reasoning as the index's.

kilobytes.description: The most kilobytes (1024 bytes) the store's records may total — the same measure `doctor`'s retirement report already prints, so the report and the rail cannot disagree about what was measured. A positive integer, on the same terms as `lines`.

librarian.description: Optional, added in 2.4. What the SCHEDULED librarian pass nags about, and after how long. Distinct from `memory` above in the way a rail is distinct from a reminder: those budgets are byte-checked by a verify recipe on every pull request and a breach is red, while everything here is measured from git history and produces a draft for a human, never a verdict. That split is not a preference — a check that reads history is a false-red generator in a shallow checkout, so the recipe never asks and the scheduled pass always may. A workspace may declare a store and no pass, which is every workspace before 2.4; what it may not do is declare this object without `slots.memory`, since there would be nothing to age. That conditional requirement is `doctor`'s, not the schema's — the declared subset has no `dependentRequired`, exactly as with `memory` at 2.3 and `tree` when `kind` is `repository`.

staleness.description: Optional. The three intervals the pass nags on. Nothing here is defaulted, on the same reasoning as the memory budgets: a default would be this specification setting cadence policy for every workspace that adopts it, in a key nobody typed — and an undeclared interval means the pass reports the facts and flags nothing, which is a legitimate way to run it. How OFTEN the pass runs is deliberately not declarable here: that is the host's scheduler rather than the workspace's content, and a cron expression in a manifest nothing reads would be configuration pretending to be policy.

record_days.description: How long a memory record may go untouched before the pass flags it as stale and drafts a demotion for it. Measured from the record's last AUTHOR date in git — author rather than committer, because a rebase rewrites every committer date and would report the whole store as touched on the day of the last rebase. A positive integer: the declared subset has no `minimum`, so `type: number` is the strongest constraint expressible here, and `cli/librarian.mjs` refuses zero, negative and non-integer values with exit 2 rather than reading them as undeclared.

sealed_days.description: How long a SEALED provenance stamp stands before its owner is nagged to re-validate it. Dated from the stamp's own `date=`, never from the file's last commit: the stamp records when the incident was sealed, and a typo fix must not buy it another interval. This is the nag `docs/vision.md` thesis 4 names in as many words — the librarian cannot judge a sealed rule, so it asks the owner instead. A positive integer, on the same terms as `record_days`.

proposal_days.description: How long a proposal may sit undecided before the pass nags. Requires `slots.proposals`; without it the pass reports that it was not asked, which is not the same answer as none pending. A positive integer, on the same terms as `record_days`.

slug.description: A lowercase hyphenated identifier. Defined once and referenced everywhere an id is used or named, so the constraint cannot drift between the field that declares an id and the field that points at one.

path.description: A relative path to a file or directory, resolved from the workspace root. The leading character may not be `/` (no absolute paths) and `:` is excluded (no URLs), so `../` is the only way out of the workspace — which is deliberate, since escaping should be visible in the value itself.

filePath.description: A relative path to a file — same rules as `path`, and must not end in `/`.

dirPath.description: A relative path to a directory — same rules as `path`, and must end in `/`, so the intent is legible without touching the filesystem.

recipe.description: One verify recipe: what to run, and what it needs in order to run at all.

run.description: The command, as it would be typed from the repository root.

requires.description: The tools the recipe needs. Declared rather than discovered, because a recipe that cannot run must be distinguishable from one that ran and failed — the difference between exit 2 and exit 1.

doc.description: Where the recipe's checks and their known limits are written up. Resolved from the WORKSPACE root, like every other path in this manifest — unlike the sibling `run`, which is a command line and is therefore written as it would be typed from the repository root. The two bases differ because the two fields are read by different things: `doc` by something resolving paths, `run` by a shell.

name.description: Display name, when it differs from the id.

product.description: The product layer: mission, what it is, why it exists.

affordances.description: What this product offers an agent working on it — entry points, commands, machine-readable contracts, and the honest gaps. Overrides the workspace-level default.

repos.description: The `repos/` card names this product ships from.

provenance.description: How a rule links to the incident that created it. NOT a manifest key — rules live in Markdown records (memory entries, proposals), and this is the normative shape their `provenance:` field is parsed into. One definition, two carriers. Adopted 2026-07-25 from .portulan/proposals/0002-sealed-provenance.md; see spec/slots.md for the reasoning and the honest limits.

oneOf.description: Public — a resolvable link to the incident: a ticket, a PR, a postmortem, a commit.

href.description: Where the incident lives: a ticket, a PR, a postmortem, a commit. Shape only — never dereferenced, because a gate that needs the network fails for reasons unrelated to the change under test. Whitespace is rejected so that `well-formed` is a claim a checker can actually enforce rather than a description of intent.

oneOf.description: Sealed — an owner and a date plus the de-identified failure shape, for an incident that cannot leave its owner's layer. The full chain stays in the owner's workspace; what travels is the stamp and the mechanism, never the episode.

owner.description: Who can still see the incident and therefore re-validate the rule.

date.description: ISO date of the incident, which is what the librarian nags against.

shape.description: The de-identified failure: the inputs, the wrong outcome, and why the obvious guard misses it. The bar is that someone who never saw the incident can still write the rule's test.
